newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends higher on fund, trade buying.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends higher on fund, trade buying.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures ended higher on Thursday in active trading supported by some trade and late session fund buying, traders said.
"The trade was buying early this (Thursday) morning," a floor source said. March cotton also exited the board.
Carl Anderson, cotton marketing specialist at Texas A&M University, said "the market remained sideways despite this lackluster weekly export sales report."

USDA on Thursday said U.S. net export sales for cotton for the week ended February 27 totaled 63,900 running bales (RB) were 72 percent below the previous week and two-thirds under the four-week average.
"There were some indications that some new sales took place at lower prices earlier this week but that will not be shown until a later report," Anderson said.
An estimated 14,000 lots changed hands up from about 5,663 lots on Wednesday, the trader said, who pegged major resistance at 77 cents, basis May. May was up 0.79 cent at 76.05 cents a pound.
But on the bearish side, Anderson said there was a large number of certificated stocks weighing on prices and the lack of trade buying above 76.00 cents.
